key: Ask which side of the basement membrane the cell sits on: theca cells live with the capillaries and make androgen under LH, while avascular granulosa cells inside use FSH-induced aromatase to finish estradiol.
items: Makes androstenedione from cholesterol under LH
a
LH drives side-chain cleavage and 17-hydroxylase activity in theca cells, which end the pathway at androgen.
Lies outside the follicle basement membrane
a
The theca forms around the follicle once it becomes secondary, outside the membrane that encloses the granulosa layers.
Has a capillary blood supply before ovulation
a
Capillaries reach the theca but not the granulosa, which is why theca cells can take up circulating cholesterol.
Expresses 17α-hydroxylase
a
This enzyme is needed to make androgens. Granulosa cells lack it and so depend on theca androstenedione.
Takes up LDL cholesterol from blood
a
With direct capillary access, theca cells import LDL cholesterol as the starting material for steroid synthesis.
Has little aromatase of its own
a
Because theca cells cannot aromatize much, their androgen must cross to the granulosa to become estradiol.
Expresses FSH-induced aromatase
b
FSH binding switches on aromatase in granulosa cells, the FSH half of the two-cell model.
Converts androstenedione to estrone and estradiol
b
Granulosa aromatase turns the diffusing androgen into estrone, which 17β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase converts to estradiol.
Secretes inhibin B
b
Granulosa inhibin B travels to the pituitary and selectively lowers FSH during the follicular phase.
Secretes anti-Müllerian hormone
b
Granulosa cells of small growing follicles make AMH, which is why AMH reflects ovarian reserve.
Forms the cumulus oophorus around the oocyte
b
The cumulus and corona radiata are granulosa cells that stay attached to the oocyte at ovulation.
Is avascular until ovulation
b
The basement membrane keeps vessels out of the granulosa layer until the follicle ruptures and luteinizes.
